priorIterationResolution.priorFinding: FIND-028 (iteration-11, critical -- clip_id derived from source URL by producer.sh can legitimately repeat across separate post attempts, making clip_id-derived tokens unsafe)
priorIterationResolution.note: Verified against /Users/anicca/anicca/skills/earn/clip/producer.sh:60-62 (clip_id remains purely source-URL-derived, unfixed, explicitly out of scope) and REQ-010 in behavioral-spec.md, which redesigned the token to be generated FRESH and RANDOM (secrets.token_hex(5)) for EACH ATTEMPT, structurally independent of clip_id/filename/source-URL. Traced concretely: even if producer.sh re-derives an identical clip_id on two separate occasions (same-day channel repeat, or a manual retry with the same --url), each separate run.sh post attempt calls the token-generation step independently and gets a cryptographically-random, attempt-scoped value -- collision no longer depends on producer.sh's own (still-absent) dedup behavior. This is a genuine structural fix, not a probabilistic mitigation.
